To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photocatalytic degradation was favored in acidic solutions, that the photocatalyst efficiency was remarkably enhanced by doping with Pt(4+), and that the incorporation of Ni2(+) was detrimental to the photocatalytic process.

the Pt-TiO (2) electrodes showed the best photocatalytic efficiency for the removal of acid red G in aqueous solutions, and the photocatalytic efficiency of the metal doped TiO( (2)) electrodes was explained on basis of the electro-affinity and the electron-work function.
The photocatalytic degradation efficiency of azo dye (AR G) by Pt-doped TiO2 thin-film electrode is higher than the efficiency of the Ni-doped and undoped TiO2 electrodes."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of the platinum- or nickel-doped multi-nanopores TiO(2)-based electrodes, which are very useful in the photocatalytic degradation process.
the production of the multi-nanopores TiO(2)-doped electrodes and their application in the photocatalytic degradation process.
the production and the application of the metal-doping of TiO(2)-based electrodes in the degradation of organic pollutants in wastewater.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TiO(2)-based electrode doped with Pt is more effective than the undoped Ti(2)O and the Ni-doped Ti(2)-based electrodes for the photocatalytic degradation and the COD reduction of acid red G.
the TiO(2)-based photocatalytic system is a promising technology for the treatment of azo dye containing effluent in wastewater.

the electrochemical method is a promising method for the production of multi-nanopores TiO(2)-based electrodes and the Pt-TiO2 electrode is a promising material for the degradation of organic compounds in aqueous solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pt-doped TiO2 thin-film electrode is more efficient than undoped TiO2 and Ni-doped TiO 2 thin-film electrodes in the degradation of azo dye in aqueous solution under UV irradiation.

the Pt-TiO2 electrode was more efficient for the removal of the COD of acid red G than the undoped Ti(2) electrode, but this efficiency was strongly dependent on the initial concentration of acid red G and the pH of the solution.
the photocatalytic activity was enhanced in the presence of platinum and was decreased in the presence of nickel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photocatalytic efficiency of the doped TiO( (2)) electrodes can be enhanced by the electroaffinity of transition metals.
the Pt-TiO2 electrode is a very good photocatalyst for the degradation of acid dye.
the Pt-TiO2 electrode is an efficient catalyst for the degradation of azo dyes in acidic media.
